title: Jackfruit Curry
subtitle: Vegan pulled jackfruit in a spiced tomato and coconut sauce
excerpt: Young green jackfruit shreds beautifully when cooked in a rich sauce, giving this vegan curry a satisfying, substantial texture. The tomato and coconut base is warming and deeply spiced, and the whole dish improves with a day in the fridge.
sourceNotes: Young green jackfruit has a fibrous texture that mimics pulled meat when cooked in a rich sauce. It is widely used across South and Southeast Asia as a vegetable curry ingredient.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the batch and freeze half.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: This curry improves with a day in the refrigerator. Reheat gently on the hob.

content.text: You will need 2 x 400g tins of young green jackfruit in brine. Drain and rinse the jackfruit, then use your hands or a fork to pull the pieces apart into shreds. Add it to the pan with the tomatoes. Avoid jackfruit in syrup: the sweet version is not right here and will make the curry cloying.

The jackfruit needs time in the sauce to absorb flavour. Do not rush the final simmer: 20 minutes of gentle cooking transforms it from a bland vegetable into one that carries the spice mix well. Fresh coriander added right at the end keeps a bright note against the richness of the coconut milk.
Drain and rinse the jackfruit thoroughly. Use your hands or a fork to pull each piece apart into coarse shreds, discarding any hard seed pods. Set aside.

Heat the oil in a large saucepan over a medium hob. Add the cumin seeds and fry for 30 seconds until they begin to pop. Add the diced onion and cook for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring regularly, until soft and starting to colour at the edges.

Add the garlic and ginger. Stir and cook for 2 minutes. Add the ground coriander, turmeric, and chilli flakes. Stir well and cook for 1 minute until the spices smell fragrant and the mixture is very dry.
Add the tinned tomatoes and stir, scraping any bits from the base of the pan. Add the shredded jackfruit and stir to coat it in the sauce. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5 minutes.

Pour in the coconut milk and stir to combine. Reduce the heat to low and simmer uncovered for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the jackfruit is very tender and the sauce has thickened around it.
Stir in the garam masala. Season well with salt. Remove from the heat and scatter over the fresh coriander. Serve with rice or flatbread.

items.symptom: The jackfruit is chewy and fibrous rather than tender
items.cause: It was not cooked in the sauce for long enough to break down.
items.fix: Add a splash of water and continue simmering with the lid on for a further 10 to 15 minutes. The jackfruit needs sustained heat in liquid to become truly tender.

items.symptom: The curry is watery and lacks body
items.cause: The coconut milk was stirred in before the tomato base had reduced enough, or the final simmer was cut short.
items.fix: Increase the heat slightly and simmer uncovered, stirring frequently, until the sauce thickens to a consistency that coats the back of a spoon.

items.cause: The spices were burnt during the dry-fry stage, or the cumin seeds were left in the hot oil too long before the onions went in.
items.fix: Keep the heat at medium when frying the spices. If the bitterness is pronounced, stir in a small pinch of sugar and an extra splash of coconut milk to balance it.

items.symptom: The sauce has a tinned, flat flavour
items.cause: The tinned tomatoes were not cooked down sufficiently to concentrate their flavour before the coconut milk was added.
items.fix: After adding the tomatoes, simmer for at least 5 minutes before pouring in the coconut milk. Season generously with salt and add garam masala only at the very end, where it gives the freshest aromatic lift.
